ledger.note: 1093: imperial immediacy. Infobox 'Established / Reichsfreiheit: 1093'; 'Wied emerged as a County earlier than many other German states'; 'located on the river Wied where it meets the Rhine'.
1243: Isenburg-Wied. 'Comital line extinct; passed to Isenburg-Wied: 1243'; 'From 1243-1462, Wied was united with an Isenburgian County as Isenburg-Wied.' Entered as a dynastic step inside one state.
1462: the Lords of Runkel. 'Inherited by Lords of Runkel and restored: 1462'. Entered as a dynastic step inside one state.
1631: Wied-Dierdorf. 'Wied was partitioned twice: between itself and Wied-Dierdorf in 1631'. Entered as a step inside one state (the page names no land).
1698: Neuwied and Runkel. 'between Wied-Neuwied and Wied-Runkel in 1698'. Entered as a step inside one state (the page names no land).

1806: mediatised. 'The county was incorporated into the Duchy of Nassau in 1806 and into the Kingdom of Prussia at the Congress of Vienna in 1815' (infobox 'Both parts mediatised to Nassau-Weilburg: 1806').

certainty.note: The page gives no area or boundary; the circle is a stand-in.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Wied row.

SCOPE. 1093 to 1806; the page is silent on wars, on rank changes and on any territory. The partitions of 1631 and 1698 are kept inside one state (rule 2). After 1806 the page gives the Duchy of Nassau, then Prussia in 1815 and Rhineland-Palatinate since 1946.

SHAPES. A 16 km circle at 7.47E 50.50N. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Neuwied', 'Dierdorf', 'Runkel'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) No area or town list; (2) the infobox gives Nassau-Weilburg and the lead the Duchy of Nassau for 1806 (the Cliopatria row Duchy of Nassau begins in 1806).
